AI Simulation Lab

Eight working machine-learning models you can run, break and argue with — built around the pain points that MAHAGENCO's own June 2026 regulatory filing exposes. Everything runs in this browser. No internet, no installation, no login. The algorithms are real; the plant data is either the actual June 2026 figures or physics-based synthetic data whose generating equations are stated in each module.

Read this first. These are teaching instruments. They run genuine algorithms on realistic data at small scale. They are not plant models, they are not validated, and no output from them should ever influence an operating decision. What they are good for is understanding how these methods behave — where they help, and exactly how they fail.

How to work through the lab. Each module opens in its default state showing the problem as it exists today. Move one control at a time and watch the numbers. Every module has a What just happened panel that explains the mechanism in engineering language, and a Where this is simpler than your plant panel that tells you what has been left out.
On the money figures. Rupee values are computed from each station's own MERC merit-order variable charge divided by its own actual net heat rate, giving a station-specific cost of heat. Nashik's heat is worth ₹0.002133/kcal; Khaperkheda Unit 5's is ₹0.001337/kcal. The same technical improvement is worth roughly sixty per cent more at Nashik than at Khaperkheda.
SIM-1 · Monitoring & maintenance

Residual anomaly detection — ID fan bearing

Why a model that knows what the bearing should be running at finds a fault weeks before a fixed threshold does — and what destroys that advantage.

The problem. A DCS alarm fires at a fixed number. That number has to be set high enough not to nuisance-trip at full load on a May afternoon, which makes it blind at forty per cent load on a January night. By the time it operates, most of the P–F interval is gone. Availability shortfall cost MAHAGENCO ₹100.87 crore of disallowed fixed charge; a large part of that is unplanned.

What just happened

Where this is simpler than your plant. One bearing, four input signals and a clean physical relationship. A real ID fan model uses thirty to sixty tags, has to cope with a second fan starting and stopping, damper and blade-pitch changes, an APH that fouls over the same period, and a historian whose compression settings may already have thrown away the slow drift you are trying to see.
SIM-2 · Performance & efficiency

Heat rate loss attribution

The June 2026 net heat-rate gap was worth ₹56 crore in one month. This module splits that gap into the part that belongs to the boiler and turbine and the part that belongs to the auxiliary switchgear — and shows that the answer is completely different at different stations.

The identity everything rests on. Generated (gross) heat rate = net heat rate × (1 − auxiliary fraction). Rearranged, it tells you whether a station's heat-rate penalty is a combustion problem or an electrical one. Nashik's boiler and turbine are beating the norm; its entire penalty is auxiliary power. Koradi Units 8-10 are the opposite.

Whole fleet, June 2026 — where the gap sits station by station

Positive bar = the boiler and turbine are worse than the norm. Negative bar = they are better, and the whole penalty is auxiliary power.

Never add these two together. Net heat rate already contains auxiliary power. The ₹56 crore net gap and the ₹33 crore auxiliary gap are not additive — the second is a component of the first. Adding them double-counts about ₹33 crore, and any business case that does so will not survive the first conversation with the finance department.
SIM-3 · Performance & efficiency

Auxiliary power optimiser

MAHAGENCO burned 81.5 million units above normative auxiliary consumption in June 2026 — worth about ₹33 crore at each station's own variable charge. Much of it is a scheduling problem, not an equipment problem.

The problem. How many mills, how many CW pumps, which fan control mode, how many ESP fields? On most shifts the answer is "whatever the last shift left running". Every combination has a different auxiliary power draw and a different effect on heat rate — more CW pumps cost auxiliary power but improve back pressure. It is a small optimisation problem that a computer solves exactly and habit solves badly.

Operating point

500 MW class unit
Drives the ESP field requirement

What the shift is running now

0 damper · 1 IGV · 2 variable speed

Auxiliary power by equipment — as run against optimised

The search

Every feasible combination is evaluated on total cost — auxiliary power plus the heat-rate consequence — and ranked. Infeasible combinations are rejected by constraint, not by preference.

What just happened

Where this is simpler than your plant. Real constraints include mill maintenance schedules, coal quality varying between bunkers, CW pump changeover restrictions, ESP hopper heater loads, ash handling cycles, and the fact that a mill start is not free. This model assumes changeovers are costless and instantaneous. They are not — a real optimiser must include switching cost or it will chatter.
SIM-4 · Fuel

Coal GCV soft sensor

As-fired GCV across MAHAGENCO's stations ranged from 2,733 to 3,270 kcal/kg in June 2026, and between 619 and 941 kcal/kg was lost between the loading and unloading ends. The lab result arrives after the shift has already made its decisions. A soft sensor fills the gap.

The problem. You cannot control what you learn about a day late. A soft sensor is a model trained on the lab results you already have, which then estimates as-fired GCV every minute from signals the plant already measures. It does not replace the laboratory — it interpolates between laboratory results.

What just happened

Where this is simpler than your plant. Real coal changes source, and a model trained on one supply will mislead you on another — this is the single biggest failure mode of a GCV soft sensor. Real sampling has its own bias. Real mills wear, which changes the relationship the model learned. Any deployed soft sensor needs a standing comparison against the laboratory and a retraining trigger when the source changes.
SIM-5 · Monitoring & maintenance

Predictive maintenance and remaining useful life

Availability shortfall cost MAHAGENCO ₹100.87 crore of disallowed fixed charge. This module turns a degradation trend into the only question a planner actually needs answered: will it reach the next planned outage, and what does it cost if it does not?

The problem. A point estimate of remaining life is almost useless — "the bearing has 62 days left" invites either complacency or panic. What a maintenance planner needs is a probability: the chance this machine survives to the outage already in the plan. That is a different question, and it has a different answer.

The decision, in money

What just happened

Where this is simpler than your plant. A single monotonic degradation mode with a known failure threshold. Real machines have several competing damage mechanisms, a threshold nobody has ever measured, step changes at every intervention, and a health index that resets when a sensor is replaced. The uncertainty band here is honest about statistical error only — it says nothing about the model being the wrong model, which is usually the larger risk.
SIM-6 · Performance & efficiency

Combustion multi-objective optimiser

Koradi Units 8-10 ran a gross heat rate of 2,272 kcal/kWh against a normative 2,096 — a 176 kcal/kWh gap on 964.8 MU, the single largest thermodynamic loss in the fleet in June 2026. Combustion optimisation is the most established closed-loop AI application in thermal generation, and also the one that needs the most engineering around it.

The problem. There is no single best combustion setting. Lowering excess O₂ improves heat rate and lowers NOx, but raises unburnt carbon and CO and can destabilise the flame. Raising over-fire air lowers NOx but raises unburnt carbon. It is a trade-off surface, and where you choose to sit on it is a management decision about the relative price of fuel, of a NOx penalty and of ash saleability — not a technical one.

Manual setpoints

What matters to management

The trade-off surface — every feasible setting, and where you are on it

Each point is one feasible combination of O₂, tilt, over-fire air and mill bias. The lower-left frontier is the Pareto set — settings where you cannot improve heat rate without worsening NOx. Everything above and right of it is simply wasteful.

Outcome at the current settings

What just happened

The engineering that makes this safe. Clamps on every bias the system can write. Rate limits so no change is faster than an operator would make it. A watchdog that returns the DCS to base control if the optimiser stops responding. Bumpless transfer in and out. A clearly marked operator override. If a vendor cannot describe all five for their system, they are not ready to connect to your DCS. Switch the clamps off above and watch what an unconstrained optimiser proposes.
SIM-7 · Generative AI

RAG — grounding AI in your own documents

Retrieval-augmented generation is the difference between a party trick and a plant tool. This module runs a real retrieval engine over an indexed corpus of plant documents and shows you exactly what the model would be given before it answers.

The problem. A public chatbot answers from what it half-remembers of the internet. It has never read your OEM manual, your SOPs or your trip reports — and it will not tell you that. It will produce a clearance figure with total confidence and no source. RAG changes the order of operations: search your documents first, then answer only from what was found, and cite it.

What just happened

Honest about this demo. The retrieval is real — TF-IDF term weighting with cosine similarity, plus optional exact keyword matching for tag numbers and equipment codes, running in this browser over an indexed corpus. The answer generation is templated from the retrieved passages, because there is no language model inside this file. In a real deployment a language model writes that paragraph from the same retrieved text. What this demo shows faithfully is the part that determines whether the answer is trustworthy: what gets retrieved, how it is scored, and whether it is cited.
SIM-8 · Agentic AI

Agentic engineering assistant

An agent is a model given tools, a goal and permission to decide the order in which to use them. This module walks a real triage scenario step by step, showing every tool call, what came back, and what the agent concluded — and stops at the point where an engineer has to sign.

The scenario. 06:40. A residual monitoring model raises an advisory on Koradi Unit 8 — ID fan A drive-end bearing, 4.6 °C above expected, sustained for six days. Today that alert lands in an inbox and waits for somebody to have time. Watch what an agent does with it in ninety seconds.

The rule that does not bend. An agent may hold read-only credentials to the historian, the CMMS and the document store. It must never hold a credential that can write to the DCS, change a protection setting, or close a permit. Every write goes through a named human. Switch on write access above and read what it says.

Station performance, June 2026

The decomposition — auxiliary power against boiler and turbine

Gross heat rate = net heat rate × (1 − auxiliary fraction). A negative gross gap means the boiler and turbine are beating the norm and the whole penalty is auxiliary power.

Fuel economics, derived from each station's own merit-order variable charge

Cost of heat = MOD variable charge ÷ actual net heat rate. Implied as-fired coal cost = cost of heat × as-fired GCV. This is the station's own money, not an assumption.

Value at stake, June 2026

Do not add columns 2 and 4. Net heat rate already contains auxiliary power; the auxiliary figure is a component of the heat-rate figure, not an addition to it.

What this data does not tell you. One month is not a trend, and June is a low-demand-season month. Normative values are regulatory constructs, not thermodynamic optima. The filing does not separate planned overhaul from forced outage inside the availability figure. Heat rate is a monthly average across a group of units, so a single poor unit hides inside a group number. And auxiliary consumption is structurally higher at low PLF, so part of the auxiliary gap at Chandrapur 3-7 and Khaperkheda 1-4 is a consequence of being backed down rather than of inefficiency — separating those two is itself a worthwhile analytics project.
